objective: By the end of the lesson, learners will have practiced and developed the sub-skills of reading for gist and detailed comprehension in the context of Indonesian food and food culture.
materials:
- Skillful 2, pp.28-30
- YouTube video: Eating Giant Frogs in Indonesia (1 min lead-in)

stages.stage_aim: To spark curiosity about Indonesian food culture through an engaging video and activate prior knowledge
stages.procedure: Play the first minute of a YouTube video showing people eating giant frogs in Indonesia. In pairs, learners discuss what they saw, what it suggests about Indonesian food culture, and what they already know about Indonesian cuisine. Elicit ideas as a class and connect responses to the lesson topic.

stages.stage_aim: To introduce key vocabulary needed to understand the reading text
stages.procedure: Learners complete Exercise A (Vocabulary preview) individually, matching the eight words with their definitions. Check answers in pairs, then conduct whole-class feedback.

stages.stage_aim: To get the general idea of the text and identify its main topics
stages.procedure: Learners look at the picture and heading, then answer Exercise B (Before you read), identifying the text's purpose. They skim the text for Exercise C1, checking which topics are mentioned. Learners then complete the summary in Exercise C2 using their answers. Quick pair-check before feedback.

stages.stage_aim: To extract specific information and distinguish between stated, false, and unstated information
stages.procedure: Learners read the text again more carefully and complete Exercise D (Close reading), deciding whether each sentence is True, False, or Not Given. Encourage learners to underline supporting evidence in the text for each answer. Peer-check in pairs before class feedback with justification.

stages.stage_aim: To discuss ideas from the reading and relate them to personal experience
stages.procedure: In small groups, learners discuss Exercise E (Critical thinking), focusing on dietary changes in Indonesia and their own country, and the health implications of processed food. Whole-class feedback on key discussion points with brief content and language correction.
